ImageDescription.value:
Mini (BMW Group) in the Dernekamp hamlet, Kirchspiel, Dülmen, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
The Mini dates back to the classic Mini from 1959, which was developed by Alec Issigonis for the British Motor Corporation. With its transversely mounted engine and front-wheel drive, it was revolutionary in terms of space efficiency and became a cult car of the 1960s.
After several changes of ownership, BMW took over the brand and launched a modern reissue in 2001. The new Mini was larger and safer, but retained the retro design with round headlights and a contrasting roof.
The modern Mini stands for compact size, a sporty “go-kart feeling”, individual design options, and modern technology—from the classic 3-door model to the electric version.

ImageDescription.value:
Eruption of the Old Faithful Geyser in Yellowstone National Park, Wyoming, USA
Yellowstone National Park was founded on March 1, 1872, and is considered the world’s first national park. It is located primarily in the state of Wyoming, but also extends into Montana and Idaho. The initiative to establish the park was based on scientific expeditions from 1869 to 1871, which documented the unique landscape. President Ulysses S. Grant signed the protection law.
The park covers approximately 8,983 km² and is located on a massive volcanic hotspot. About half of all geysers worldwide are found here. The Old Faithful geyser, which erupts approximately every 90 minutes, is famous. In addition to geysers, hot springs, mud pots, and the colorful Grand Prismatic Spring characterize the area.
Yellowstone is also an important wildlife refuge. Since the reintroduction of wolves in 1995, it has been considered a model project for nature conservation. The park attracts several million visitors annually and has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1978.

ImageDescription.value:
Photo art based on a picture of a rolling gate of Gas Cleaning West at blast furnace 5 in the Landschaftspark Duisburg-Nord, Duisburg, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
The shot was created by intentional moving the camera (intentional camera movement, ICM) and subsequent composition using copies of the same shot.
The Landschaftspark Duisburg-Nord (also known as “LaPaNo” or “LaPaDu” for short) is a landscape park covering around 180 hectares surrounding a disused steelworks in Duisburg-Meiderich. The former plant was founded in 1902 by August Thyssen as a “joint-stock company for metallurgical operations” to supply his Siemens-Martin steelworks in Bruckhausen and Styrum, and went into operation on May 16, 1903, with the firing up of blast furnace 1. In 1985, blast furnace 5 was shut down after just twelve years of operation due to overcapacity on the European steel market, making it the last remaining blast furnace. In the 1990s, the halls, buildings, and outdoor areas were redesigned according to plans by architects Peter Latz + Partner. In 1994, the park was opened to the public.
